result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would remove chronic scarcity of basic needs and opportunity — make sure every person has reliable access to nutritious food, clean water, basic healthcare, safe shelter, and high-quality education and the freedom to use it.

Why: so many global problems—conflict, poor health, short-term thinking, exploitation, lack of creativity—stem from unmet basic needs. When people aren’t constantly fighting to survive, they can invest in learning, care for others, innovate, and plan for the future. Guaranteeing those foundations would amplify people’s ability to solve climate, governance, and cultural challenges themselves.

The change isn’t just material: it would shift incentives and relationships, increasing stability, cooperation, and dignity worldwide. That one transformation would cascade into better health, stronger communities, more equitable opportunity, and far more room for human potential.
